East Defensive Player of the Year]] (2007) * Third-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (2005) }} '''Jerel McNeal''' (born June 1, 1987) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball|Marquette University]] before playing professionally in Belgium, the [[NBA G League|NBA D-League]], Italy, China, Greece, Germany and Israel, including a short stint in the [[NBA]] with the [[Phoenix Suns]] in 2014. ==Early life== McNeal was born in [[Chicago]], Illinois to parents Edward and Meryln McNeal. He has 2 siblings (January and Jeremy). He attended [[Hillcrest High School (Illinois)|Hillcrest High School]] along with point guard [[Maurice Acker]], an eventual college teammate. McNeal was a third-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] in 2005. == College career == McNeal won the [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Defensive Player of the Year|Big East's Defensive Player of the Year]] award as a sophomore in the 2006–07 season and was the only guard on the Big East's All-First Team in 2008–09. McNeal was an [[2009 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|Associated Press second team All-American]] in 2008–09 as well. On February 10, 2009, in a 102–84 loss at [[Villanova Wildcats|Villanova]], McNeal broke George Thompson's 41-year-old school record of 1,773 points. Markus Howard passed McNeal for the Marquette scoring record, but McNeal remains Marquette's all-time leader in steals, field goals made, and field goal attempts. He is third all-time in games played and seventh in assists.[http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/marq/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2012-13/misc_non_event/201213_mbb_recordbook.pdf MARQUETTE MEN’S BASKETBALL RECORD BOOK] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304211313/http://grfx.cstv.com/photos/schools/marq/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/2012-13/misc_non_event/201213_mbb_recordbook.pdf |date=2016-03-04 }} ==Professional career== ===2009–10 season=== After going undrafted in the [[2009 NBA draft]], McNeal joined the [[Sacramento Kings]] for the 2009 [[NBA Summer League|Las Vegas Summer League]]. On September 28, 2009, he signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. However, he was waived on October 19, 2009. In November 2009, he signed with [[Belfius Mons-Hainaut|Dexia Mons-Hainaut]] of Belgium for the 2009–10 season. In March 2010, he left Dexia after drawing a two-week suspension for a positive marijuana test.[http://www.sportando.net/eng/europa/esteri/7065/jerel_mcneal_leaves_dexia_mons_hainaut.html Jerel McNeal leaves Dexia Mons-Hainaut] ===2010–11 season=== In July 2010, he joined the Charlotte Bobcats for the Orlando Summer League{{Cite web |url=http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2010/6/28/1540821/nba-summer-league-rosters-orlando |title=NBA Summer League Rosters - Orlando |access-date=June 30, 2010 |archive-date=June 30, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100630183256/http://www.ridiculousupside.com/2010/6/28/1540821/nba-summer-league-rosters-orlando |url-status=dead }} and the Chicago Bulls for the Las Vegas Summer League. On October 9, 2010, he signed with the Houston Rockets. However, he was waived by the Rockets on October 18. On October 30, 2010, he was acquired by the Rio Grande Valley Vipers. On March 9, 2011, he signed a 10-day contract with the New Orleans Hornets.[http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets_sign_jerel_mcnel___2011_03_09.html Hornets sign Jerel McNeal to a 10-day contract] On March 19, he returned to the Vipers after his 10-day contract expired. He did not appear in a game for the Hornets during his 10 days with the team.[http://www.nola.com/hornets/index.ssf/2011/03/new_orleans_hornets_forward_we.html New Orleans Hornets' David West bracing for double-team against Celtics] ===2011–12 season=== In July 2011, he signed with [[Sutor Basket Montegranaro]] of Italy for the 2011–12 season.[http://www.sportando.net/eng/italy/serie-a/29425/sutor-montegranaro-announces-jerel-mcneal.html Sutor Montegranaro announces Jerel McNeal] ===2012–13 season=== On September 21, 2012, McNeal signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{Cite web |url=http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/raptors-sign-mcneal-and-wright/ |title=Raptors Sign McNeal And Wright |access-date=2012-09-24 |archive-date=2014-02-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201112019/http://blog.raptors.com/press-releases/raptors-sign-mcneal-and-wright/ |url-status=dead }} However, he was waived by the Raptors on October 22.{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11242 |title=Toronto Raptors waive Jerel McNeal and Chris Wright |access-date=2012-10-24 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150908093056/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11242 |archive-date=2015-09-08 |url-status=dead }} On November 1, 2012, he was re-acquired by the Vipers. The next day, he was traded to the [[Bakersfield Jam]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/bakersfield_jam_acquire_jerel__2012_11_02.html |title=Bakersfield Jam Acquire Jerel McNeal from Vipers |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2012-11-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150320053636/http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/bakersfield_jam_acquire_jerel__2012_11_02.html |archive-date=2015-03-20 |url-status=dead }} On February 4, 2013, McNeal was named to the Prospects All-Star roster for the 2013 NBA D-League All-Star Game.[http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html 2013 NBA Development League All-Star Game Rosters Announced] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131022065410/http://www.nba.com/dleague/news/2013_nba_development_league_all_star_rosters_announced_2013_02_04.html |date=2013-10-22 }} On March 27, 2013, McNeal signed a 10-day contract with the Utah Jazz.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-signs-jerel-mcneal-10-day-contract | title= Jazz Signs Jerel McNeal to a 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com| publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.| date=March 27, 2013 |access-date=April 7, 2013}} On April 6, 2013, McNeal signed with the Utah Jazz for the rest of the 2012–13 season.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-signs-jerel-mcneal-remainder-season |title= Jazz Signs Jerel McNeal for Remainder of Season |work=NBA.com| publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.| date=April 6, 2013 |access-date=April 7, 2013}} He joined the Jazz for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. On September 25, 2013, he was waived by the Jazz before appearing in a game for them.{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14328 |title=Utah Jazz waive guard Jerel McNeal |access-date=2013-09-26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924042720/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14328 |archive-date=2015-09-24 |url-status=dead }} ===2013–14 season=== In October 2013, McNeal signed with the [[Zhejiang Golden Bulls]] for the 2013–14 season.{{Cite web |url=http://www.niubball.com/2013/10/zhejiang-fills-out-import-roster-signs-jerel-mcneal/ |title=Zhejiang fills out import roster, signs Jerel McNeal |access-date=2014-01-13 |archive-date=2015-09-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150905132310/http://www.niubball.com/2013/10/zhejiang-fills-out-import-roster-signs-jerel-mcneal/ |url-status=dead }} In December 2013, he was released by the Golden Bulls after 15 games. On February 24, 2014, he was reacquired by the Bakersfield Jam. ===2014–15 season=== On August 4, 2014, McNeal signed a one-year deal with the Spanish team [[CB Sevilla|Baloncesto Sevilla]].{{cite news|title=Sevilla adds McNeal at point|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/139991/3735|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140808060837/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/139991/3735|url-status=dead|archive-date=August Jam Guard Jerel McNeal Named 2015 NBA Development League Impact Player of the Year] On April 1, 2015, McNeal signed a 10-day contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]].[http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-jerel-mcneal-10-day-contract Suns Sign Jerel McNeal to 10-Day Contract] The following day, he made his NBA debut, scoring two points in a 107–106 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150402/PHXGSW/gameinfo.html |title=Barnes' shot lifts Warriors to 107-106 win over Suns |website=[[NBA.com]] signed with the Suns through the 2015–16 season.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/04/11/suns-sign-jerel-mcneal/ |title=Suns sign Jerel McNeal |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2015-04-12 Suns.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-teletovic-weems-price|title=Suns Sign Teletovic, Weems, Price|work=NBA.com|date=July 17, 2015|access-date=July 18, 2015}} Despite this, McNeal continued to play for the Suns at the 2015 Las Vegas Summer League, where he averaged 2.1 points and 1.3 rebounds in seven games.{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague/2015/players/sl_jerel_mcneal/ |title=2015 Summer League Player Profile – Jerel McNeal |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2015-07-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150803035531/http://www.nba.com/summerleague/2015/players/sl_jerel_mcneal |archive-date=2015-08-03 |url-status=dead }} ===2015–16 season=== On July 31, 2015, McNeal signed with [[Aris B.C.|Aris Thessaloniki]] of Greece for the 2015–16 season.{{cite news|title=Jerel McNeal inks with Aris Thessaloniki|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/171156/jerel-mcneal-inks-with-aris-thessaloniki.html|access-date=July 31, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=July 31, 2015}} In 36 league games for Aris, he averaged 14.1 points, 3.9 rebounds, 2.7 assists and 1.1 steals per game. He also appeared in 16 [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]] games, averaging 14.4 points, 4.3 rebounds, 2.2 assists and 1.6 steals per game. ===2016–17 season=== On December 21, 2016, McNeal signed a two-month contract with German club [[Brose Bamberg]].{{cite news|title=Jerel McNeal officially signs with Brose Bamberg|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/220974/jerel-mcneal-officially-signs-with-brose-bamberg.html|access-date=December 22, 2016|work=Sportando.com|date=December 21, 2016}} On February 23, 2017, he re-signed with Bamberg for the rest of the season.[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/226878/brose-bamberg-keeps-jerel-mcneal-for-the-season.html Brose Bamberg keeps Jerel McNeal for the season] ===2017–18 season=== On August 22, 2017, McNeal signed with French team [[SIG Basket|SIG Strasbourg]].[http://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba-champions-league/499374/jerel-mcneal-new-member-strasbourg/ Jerel McNeal is the new member of Strasbourg] However, on September 2, 2017, he parted ways with Strasbourg before appearing in a game for them.{{cite news|title=Strasbourg : Finalement, Jerel McNeal ne viendra pas|url=http://www.sport365.fr/basket-pro-a-strasbourg-finalement-jerel-mcneal-ne-viendra-5725297.html|access-date=November 3, 2018|work=sport365.fr|date=September 2, 2017|language=fr}} On September 30, 2017, McNeal signed a one-year deal with the Israeli team [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]].{{cite news|title=Jerel McNeal signs with Hapoel Tel Aviv|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/turkey/bsl/248490/jerel-mcneal-signs-with-hapoel-tel-aviv.html|access-date=September 30, 2017|work=Sportando.com|date=September 30, 2017}} On March 10, 2018, McNeal recorded a season-high 25 points along with eight rebounds, four assists and four steals in a 90–87 win over [[Maccabi Rishon LeZion (basketball)|Maccabi Rishon LeZion]].{{cite news|title=Winner League, Game 19: M. Rishon Vs Hapoel TA - Box Score|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=23260&lang=en|access-date=August 4, 2018|work=basket.co.il|date=March 10, 2018}} In 37 games played for Hapoel, he averaged 13.7 points, 3.3 rebounds, 4 assists and 1.9 steals per game. McNeal helped Hapoel reach the [[2018 Israeli Basketball Premier League Final Four|2018 Israeli League Final Four]], where they eventually lost to [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] in the Semifinals. ===2018–19 season=== On November 2, 2018, McNeal returned to Hapoel Tel Aviv for the [[2018–19 Israeli Basketball Premier League|2018–19 season]].{{cite news|title=Jerel McNeal returns to Hapoel Tel Aviv|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jerel-mcneal-returns-to-hapoel-tel-aviv/|access-date=November 3, 2018|work=Sportando.basketball|date=November 2, 2018|archive-date=November 3, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181103131225/https://sportando.basketball/en/jerel-mcneal-returns-to-hapoel-tel-aviv/|url-status=dead}} On April 12, 2019, McNeal participated in the [[2018–19 Israeli Basketball Premier League#All-Star Event|2019 Israeli League All-Star]] game.{{cite web|title=אולסטאר: ניצחון שלישי ברציפות לזרים|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=21081|access-date=August 3, 2019|work=basket.co.il|date=April 12, 2019|language=he}} McNeal helped Hapoel reach the [[2018–19 Israeli Basketball Premier League#Playoffs|2019 Israeli League Playoffs]], where they eventually were eliminated by [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] in the Quarterfinals. ===2019–20 season=== On September 6, 2019, McNeal signed a one-year deal with [[Ironi Nahariya]], joining his former head coach [[Danny Franco]] and teammate [[Tony Gaffney]].{{Cite news|title=Jerel McNeal joins Ironi Nahariya|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/jerel-mcneal-joins-ironi-nahariya/|date=September 6, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|access-date=September 6, 2019}} On October 28, 2019, McNeal recorded a season-high 27 points, shooting 9-of-13 from the field, along with eight rebounds and two assists in an 86–84 win over his former team [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]].{{Cite web|title=איקס על האקסית: מקניל גבר על האדומים|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=24045|date=October 28, 2019|publisher=basket.co.il|access-date=October 28, 2019|language=he}} ==The Basketball Tournament== McNeal played for the [[Golden Eagles (TBT)|Golden Eagles]] in the 2018 edition of [[The Basketball Tournament]]. In five games, he averaged 13.4 points, 5 rebounds, and 2.4 steals per game while shooting 53 percent from the field.
